The Market, from left to right.
Two slots fed by the Main deck, then one Civilised slot, one Tradition slot and one Region slot. It always holds five cards: any emptied slot is refilled at once.
Under which Market cards is an Unrest card tucked?
Under all of them
Under all except Regions
Only under the two Main deck cards
Regions never have Unrest under them; every other Market card has one.
Where does your Accession card go?
In your starting hand
At the very bottom of your Nation deck, face up
In the Development area
The Nation deck is placed crosswise on top of the Accession, which will therefore be the last card to come out.
Your turn: three orders
On your turn you announce a single order out of three, resolve it, then do your Cleanup. The player to the left of the Solstice token starts the round and play goes clockwise.
Hands-on: the three orders
Actions and Exhaust abilities in practice
Take an Action
: remove an Action token from your State card. No token left, no Action, except a Free action.
Play a card
: resolve its text as much as possible, then put it in your discard pile, unless it says to go elsewhere. Permanent cards (icon in the header) stay in play in front of you.
A card whose text starts with
Exhaust
does nothing when you put it down: it is a permanent card whose effect will be used later.

: move an Exhaust token from your State card onto a card in play (or onto your Power card) that doesn't have one yet, then resolve the text after the word Exhaust. If the ability has a cost you can't pay, you can't use it.
Some Exhaust abilities respond to an event ("when…"). They resolve right after the sentence that triggered them, before the next sentence.
Free action

: the card is played without an Action token, even if you have none left. The same card can only be played this way once per turn. Free does not mean without cost: costs written on the card are still due.
Gain an Action
: take an Action token from the supply, even if you go above three. You go back to three at Cleanup.

Your hand only holds Unrest and unplayable cards. You want a good Tradition card visible in the Market, without taking the Unrest under it. Which order?
Research: you discard your hand and Innovate a card, without the Unrest.
During a Research order, can you use an Exhaust ability?
Yes, just one
No, neither Action nor Exhaust ability
Yes, if it is free
Research and Pacify replace the whole turn. Only Passive abilities stay active.
You have used your 3 Actions. A card lets you play another one "as a Free action". Is that possible?
No, you need a token
Yes, without an Action token
Yes, by spending an Exhaust token
A Free action uses no token and remains possible with no Action token available.
Resolving a card
Cards are read literally. Nine principles settle almost every case.
Each sentence resolves separately, in order.
Each sentence resolves
as much as possible
. Whatever follows the word "may" is optional; everything else is mandatory.
If you can't resolve any part of the effect, you can't play the card.
If the text doesn't say where the card goes next, it goes to your discard pile (except permanent cards).
Whatever comes before the word "to" is a
cost
: "Do X to gain Y". You may pay a cost even if the result is uncertain or impossible.
Paying or Moving resources is always a cost, even without "to".
If a mandatory cost can't be paid in full, you can neither play the card nor trigger the effect.
The cost is paid in full before the rest of the effect.
If you pay a cost, you must resolve the result, as much as possible.

When a card offers options separated by OR, you resolve only one. A full sentence placed after the list applies whatever you chose. If the chosen option requires a payment you can't make, you must choose another.
All players.
All players or "each player" includes you. "All other players" does not.
A card marked with the Attack icon hits all other players, as much as possible. Some cards let a player ignore all or part of an Attack aimed at them.
Pay 2 Materials to Draw 2 cards. You only have 1 Material and no Progress. Can you play the card?
Yes, I pay 1 and draw 1
No: a mandatory cost must be payable in full
Yes, the cost is optional
A cost is never half-paid. If it is mandatory and unpayable, the card is unplayable.
Gain 2 Population. You may Discard a card to Draw a card. What is mandatory?
Only gaining 2 Population
Only the discard
The text after "may" is optional; the first sentence is mandatory.
A card says "All other players Recover an Unrest card". Are you affected?
All other players excludes you.
The Market: Acquire and Innovate
Two verbs to take a card, and one big difference: the Unrest.
Choose a visible Market card of the allowed category. Gain the resources placed on it. Take the card into your hand,
with the Unrest card tucked under it
. The Market is refilled at once, and an Unrest from the pile is tucked under the new card, unless it is a Region.
Announce a category, then choose: either a visible Market card (you gain its resources, the Unrest under it
goes back to the pile
), or the top face-down card of the Region, Tradition or Civilised deck. "When you Acquire" effects do not trigger.
Special cases of Innovate

Tributaries have no deck of their own. To Innovate one blind, reveal cards from the Main deck one by one until the first Tributary, take it, then shuffle the other revealed cards back into the Main deck.
Same procedure for a category whose deck is empty. As long as the Region, Tradition or Civilised deck has cards, you may not search the Main deck for that category.
If the search finds nothing, you gain 2 Progress instead.
With the Research order, you Innovate a Region, a Tradition, a Civilised or a Tributary, never a Fame card.
Replacing a taken card

A card taken from one of the first two slots is replaced from the Main deck. The others are replaced from their slot's deck, or from the Main deck if that one is empty. So a card sometimes ends up in a slot that doesn't match its category. If an effect makes you Acquire several cards, finish each acquisition, replacement included, before the next: you may take the card that just arrived.

Exile and Exchange

a Market card sends it to the Exile pile, next to the Market. The Unrest under it goes back to its pile, and the card is replaced normally. A card carrying tokens can't be Exiled. Some cards let you Acquire or Innovate from the Exile pile: if you Acquire a card other than a Region there, you must also Recover an Unrest.
Exchange

replaces a Market card with another one from elsewhere (your hand, for example). Tokens stay on the slot, the old Unrest goes back to the pile and a new one is tucked under the incoming card, except a Region. If the exchange requires "the same category", both cards must share a category icon.
You Acquire a Tradition carrying 2 Progress with an Unrest under it. What do you get?
Only the card
The card and the 2 Progress
The card, the 2 Progress and the Unrest
Acquiring gives you everything: resources to your reserve, card and Unrest to your hand.
You Innovate the same card. What happens to the Unrest?
I take it
It goes back to the Unrest pile
It goes to the Exile pile
That is the whole point of Innovating: the card without the Unrest.
The Civilised deck still has cards. Can you search the Main deck to Innovate a Civilised card?
No, not until the Civilised deck is empty
Searching the Main deck is only allowed for Tributaries or for a category whose deck is empty.
Cleanup and reshuffling the deck
It is the engine of the game, and the part of the rules people come back to most often at first.
Cleanup, in four steps
Add 1 Progress from the supply onto a Market card
of your choice. From the supply, not from your reserve. It is the most common thing to forget.
Take back your tokens
: 3 Actions and 5 Exhaust tokens back on your State card.
You may Discard
as many cards from your hand as you like.
up to your hand limit (5 by default). If you already have 5 or more cards, you don't draw, and you don't have to go back down to 5.
As soon as you have finished step 1, the next player can start their turn while you finish.
Rulebook tip.
Discard generously. The faster your deck cycles, the sooner your Nation cards, your Accession and your Developments arrive.
Shuffling your discard pile
When you must Draw and your deck is empty, you shuffle immediately, even during someone else's turn. Before shuffling, you may add
one card, only once per turn
, and you need an available Exhaust token for this, which serves as a marker:
There is a card left in your Nation deck
(Accession included): put the top one into your discard pile and place an Exhaust token on the Nation deck. If it is the Accession, flip your State card: you are now an Empire.
The Nation deck is empty

: you may Pay the cost of a card in your Development area, whichever you want, to put it into your discard pile. Then place an Exhaust token on the area. If you can't pay for any card, you don't Develop.
Shuffle your discard pile: it is your new deck.
Resolve any "when you shuffle" effects.
Keep Drawing up to your hand limit.

During Cleanup you always have a token available, since you just took them back. Mid-turn however, if all your Exhaust tokens are used or a marker is already placed, you shuffle without adding anything.
Draw, if possible
: this kind of effect never causes a shuffle. Empty deck, no draw.

Where does the Progress token you add to the Market during Cleanup come from?
From my reserve
From the supply
From a neighbouring Market card
Always from the supply. Your reserve isn't touched.
Your deck runs out mid-turn, and your 5 Exhaust tokens are already on cards. What happens?
I can't draw
I shuffle my discard pile without adding a Nation card
I add a Nation card anyway
With no Exhaust token available to serve as a marker, nothing is added. The shuffle still happens.
Your Accession card joins your discard pile. What is the immediate consequence?
The game ends
I flip my State card: I become an Empire
I draw a Fame card
The Accession flips your State card from Barbarian to Empire (the Vikings are an exception, see the Nations chapter).
The Solstice
The Solstice closes each round. When the last player has finished their turn, everyone resolves their Solstice effects.
Each player resolves
the Solstice effects in their play area, on their Power card and, if relevant, on their State card.
They are mandatory, resolved as much as possible, unless they say "may".
Everyone resolves at the same time. If order matters (often when a Collapse looms), resolve in turn order.
When you have several effects, you decide their order.
A Solstice effect that concerns "each other player" is resolved by each of them during their own Solstice, at the moment they choose among their effects.
An effect marked
End of Solstice
(a keyword introduced with Horizons) resolves after all your other Solstice effects.
During the Solstice, no Action and no Exhaust ability.
Passive abilities stay active.
Then a new round starts with the player to the left of the Solstice token.
